answers.quote: Sasanka had become the master of the whole of Bengal with his capital at Karnasuvarna (near Murshidabad), and had perhaps extended his rule as far as Orissa. He even advanced against Kanauj which was occupied by the rulers of the Maukhari dynasty at that time.
answers.notes: Capital at Karnasuvarna per claim.

answers.quote: Gopala, who went on to become the founder of the Pala dynasty in Bengal, consolidated his rule over Bengal and brought the much needed stability and prosperity to the region.
answers.notes: Gopala founder of Pala dynasty.

answers.quote: Apart from his military campaigns, Dharmpala is also known for his patronage of Buddhism. He founded many Buddhist monasteries but, it was the famous Vikramshila University founded by him, that earned him a lot of fame.
answers.notes: Dharmapala founded Vikramshila.

answers.quote: Of the Pala kings, both Dharmpala and Devapala, won fame and glory thorugh their victories in the famous Tripartite struggle. This was a struggle amongst the Pratiharas, Palas and Rashtrakutas for gaining victory over the imperial capital of Kanauj and for establishing control over Northern India.
answers.notes: Tripartite parties per claim.

answers.quote: Of the Pala kings, both Dharmpala and Devapala, won fame and glory thorugh their victories in the famous Tripartite struggle. This was a struggle amongst the Pratiharas, Palas and Rashtrakutas for gaining victory over the imperial capital of Kanauj and for establishing control over Northern India.
answers.notes: Struggle for imperial capital Kanauj.

answers.quote: In south, Dantidurga was the founder of the dynasty called, Rashtrakuta dynasty (8th AD). The capital of the Rastrakutas was Manyakheta or Malkhed near Sholapur.
answers.notes: Dantidurga founder of Rashtrakutas.

answers.quote: One of the important kings of the Rashtrakuta dynasty was Krishna I. He built the famous Kailasha temple at Ellora (near Aurangabad, Maharastra). It is dedicated to Lord Shiva and is monolithic i.e. made of one single piece of rock.
answers.notes: Krishna I built Kailasha temple.

answers.quote: The Cholas came to power after over throwing the authority of the Pallavas in South India. The founder of the Chola dynasty was Vijayalaya (9th century AD) but the real architects of the glory of the dynasty were Rajaraja I (AD 985–AD 1014) and his son Rajendra I (AD 1014–AD 1044).
answers.notes: Vijayalaya founder of Chola dynasty.

answers.quote: Important works composed in Sanskrit around this period were the kathasaritasagara a collection of stories, the Rajtarangini, a vivid account of the kings of Kashmir composed by Kalhana and the Gita Govinda, a piece of devotional literature
answers.notes: Rajatarangini composed by Kalhana.

answers.quote: Some of the outstanding examples of this style, are the Lingaraja temple at Bhuvaneshwar, the Sun temple at Konark and the Kandariya Mahadeva temple, built by the Chandella kings at Khajuraho.
answers.notes: Kandariya built by Chandella kings.

answers.quote: Sasanka’s military adventures proved successful and this ultimately led to the growth of hostilities between him and the rulers of Thanesar. Harshavardhana, who eventually became king of Thanesar, set out to defeat Sasanka but was unsuccessful. Ultimately, Harsha succeeded in his conquest of Sasanka’s empire only after the latter’s death.
answers.notes: Harsha succeeded only after Sasanka's death.

answers.quote: His brotherinlaw was the ruler of Kanauj (see Map 7) and he was killed by the ruler of Bengal. Harsha took over the kingdom of Kanauj, and then led an army against the ruler of Bengal.
answers.notes: Brother-in-law killed by ruler of Bengal.

answers.quote: The most celebrated name associated with Vikramashila University was that of Atisha Dipankara who was greatly respected in Tibet.
answers.notes: Most celebrated name at Vikramashila.

answers.quote: One of the kings of this empire, built a monastery at Nalanda in the ninth century, and at his request the Pala king Devapala of Bengal granted five villages for its upkeep.
answers.notes: Devapala granted five villages at Shailendra request.

answers.quote: The Rashtrakuta king Dhruva having crossed the Vindhyas, first defeated the Pratihara king Vatsaraja and then advanced upon Dharmpala and defeated him. With this encounter which took place somewhere in the Ganga Yamuna doab, began the Tripartite struggle for supremacy between the Palas, Pratiharas and Rashtrakutas.
answers.notes: Struggle began with Dhruva's encounter.

answers.quote: He managed to capture Kanauj and place his own nominee on the throne. He held a great imperial assembly in the presence of a large number of vassal kings at Kanauj.
answers.notes: Dharmapala captured Kanauj, placed nominee.

answers.quote: One of the important kings of this dynasty was Mihira Bhoja (ninth century). He was highly praised by an Arabian scholar Sulaiman for keeping his empire safe from robbers.
answers.notes: Sulaiman praised Mihira Bhoja.

answers.quote: Some of the vassal chiefs rose against him. Mahipala II tried to resist these vassals, but was defeated and killed. Divya, an official who belonged to the Kaivarta caste established control over North Bengal.
answers.notes: Divya established control over North Bengal.

answers.quote: Even while Madanapala was busy defending his kingdom from invasions, a new dynasty called the Senas rose in West Bengal. The first significant ruler of this dynasty was Vijayasena, who defeated Madanapala and conquered Bengal. He advanced as far as Assam and Mithila and also conquered a part of Magadha
answers.notes: First significant Sena ruler.

answers.quote: Vijayasena was succeeded by his son Ballalasena. Ballalasena who was a powerful king as well as a learned scholar, was succeeded by his son Lakshmanasena. Lakshmanasena whose reign began in 1178 A.D., had an illustrious military career. Lakshmanasena was also a learned scholar and a patron of poets.
answers.notes: Lakshmanasena reign began 1178 AD.

answers.answer: পরাজিত রাজা, যিনি অধীনতা ও করের শর্তে রাজ্য ফিরে পেয়েছেন
answers.quote: Well the term ‘Samanta’ basically refers to a king who has been defeated but his kingdom has been restored to him but with the condition that he will continue to accept the over lordship of the conquering king and also pay regular tribute to him in cash or kind.
answers.notes: Samanta definition per NIOS claim.

answers.quote: The bestknown Chalukya ruler was Pulakeshin II. We know about him from a prashasti, composed by his court poet Ravikirti.
answers.notes: Prashasti by court poet Ravikirti.

answers.quote: By the early 10th century CE, the Pallava rule came to an end when Aparajata was defeated by Aditya Chola-I.
answers.notes: Aparajita defeated by Aditya Chola I.

answers.quote: One of the greatest contribution of Rajaraja I was the construction of the famous temple known as Rajarajeshwara or Brihadesvara temple, dedicated to Shiva at Tanjore. He also ordered a survey of land for better collection of land revenue in his empire.
answers.notes: Brihadesvara dedicated to Shiva, built by Rajaraja I.

answers.quote: The three types of temple architecture which evolved during the period are known as the Nagara, Dravida and Vesara (mixed) styles during this period. The garbhagriha was the inner sanctum that housed the chiefdeity to whom the temple was dedicated. An important example of this style is the Brihadishvara temple built by Chola king Rajaraja at Tanjore.
answers.notes: not covered by claims — claims name the three styles and garbhagriha but never list vimana/gopuram/shikhara as Dravida features; shikhara is the Nagara feature, chosen as best answer.

answers.answer: তিনি প্রায় ৪০ বছর রাজত্ব করেন এবং উৎকল ও কামরূপ জয় করেন
answers.quote: Dharmpala was succeeded by his son Devapala who ruled for about 40 years.
answers.notes: 40-year rule (c22) and Utkala/Kamarupa conquest (c23).

answers.answer: তিনি ধর্মপালের মনোনীত প্রার্থীকে ও পরে ধর্মপালকে যুদ্ধে হারান
answers.quote: The Pratiharas managed to recover under the leadership of Nagabhatta, the son and successor of Vatsaraja. Nagabhatta attacked and defeated the nominee whom Dharmpala had placed on the throne of Kanauj, which resulted in a conflict with Dharmpala himself. In a battle fought against Dharmpala, Nagabhatta emerged victorious.
answers.notes: Nagabhatta (II) of c21 fits stem in tripartite context; founder-in-Malwa option is also defensible if read as Nagabhatta I (c44).

answers.answer: কালচুরি, চোল ও চালুক্য আক্রমণ ঠেকিয়ে রাজ্য রক্ষা এবং কাম্বোজদের হাত থেকে ভূখণ্ড পুনরুদ্ধার
answers.quote: Around the same time, the Chola king Rajendra Chola and a Chalukya king also invaded the Pala territories. It goes to the credit of Mahipala I, the reigning Pala king of the time, to have defended his kingdom successfully against the Kalachuris, Cholas and Chalukyas and also to have recovered territories from the Kambojas.
answers.notes: Mahipala I defence and recovery per claim.

answers.answer: গ্রামগুলি এক ও দশের এককে ভাগ ছিল, দায়িত্বে ছিলেন গ্রামপতি ও দশগ্রামিক
answers.quote: Villages under the Palas were grouped into units of one and ten under the charge of Gramapati and Dasagramika. They were royal officials responsible for the administration for these units.
answers.notes: Village units per c31; grants were permanent and also to Buddhist monasteries (c30), ruling out two distractors; sub-infeudation option is not mentioned in claims.

answers.quote: From some explicit information, it may be said that during the 7th and 8th centuries CE several new Brahman settlements called Brahmadeyas were created by the rulers for the sake of Brahmans. This in one way gave a fillip to the extension of agricultural land with irrigation facilities, generally tank irrigation.
answers.notes: Brahmadeyas gave fillip to extension of agricultural land with tank irrigation.

answers.answer: তিনি চালুক্য ভূখণ্ডে ঢুকে বাদামিতে প্রবেশ করেন এবং শ্রীলঙ্কায় দুটি নৌ-অভিযান পাঠান
answers.quote: The Pallava king Narasimha I (630-68 CE) son and successor of Mahendra I proved an equal match to the Chalukyan king and after a series of battles he took his forces into the Chalukya territory and even entered into Badami where he got inscribed on rock an inscription of victory. After this the Pallava king sent two naval expeditions to Sri Lanka to help the Sri Lankan prince Manavarma in succession struggle.
answers.notes: Narasimha I entered Badami, sent two naval expeditions.

answers.quote: The last important Chola king was Kullotunga (AD 1070–1122 AD). Under him the Chola empire started disintegrating and shrunk to much smaller area.
answers.notes: Under Kulottunga empire started disintegrating.

answers.answer: চোলরা মালদ্বীপ, লাক্ষাদ্বীপ ও শ্রীলঙ্কা জয় করে এবং মালয়, জাভা ও সুমাত্রার রাজাদের হারায়
answers.quote: The Chola Kings made a successful use of their navy and conquered not only Maldive and Lakshdweep Islands but also Sri Lanka. They also defeated the kings of Malaya and Java and Sumatra.
answers.notes: Chola navy conquests per claim.

answers.quote: Some of the outstanding examples of this style, are the Lingaraja temple at Bhuvaneshwar, the Sun temple at Konark and the Kandariya Mahadeva temple, built by the Chandella kings at Khajuraho.
answers.notes: Sun temple Konark listed among Nagara examples; Brihadishvara is Dravida (c61), Kandariya is a Nagara example (c60).

answers.answer: তিনি কনৌজ দখল করে সেখানে স্থায়ী রাজধানী স্থানান্তর করেন
answers.quote: Sasanka had become the master of the whole of Bengal with his capital at Karnasuvarna (near Murshidabad), and had perhaps extended his rule as far as Orissa. He even advanced against Kanauj which was occupied by the rulers of the Maukhari dynasty at that time.
answers.notes: Claims say capital was Karnasuvarna and he only advanced against Kanauj; permanent capital shift is unsupported/false. Other options match c13/c14.

answers.quote: Of the Pala kings, both Dharmpala and Devapala, won fame and glory thorugh their victories in the famous Tripartite struggle. This was a struggle amongst the Pratiharas, Palas and Rashtrakutas for gaining victory over the imperial capital of Kanauj and for establishing control over Northern India.
answers.notes: Centre Kanauj true; participants were Palas/Pratiharas/Rashtrakutas, not Cholas.

answers.quote: In times of war the samantas were obliged to render military aid to the suzerain. The Harshcharit of Banabhatt elaborately discusses the role of the Samantas. It seems that tributary relationship was the keynote of the Samant (feudatory) system.
answers.notes: Military aid duty (c34); samantas tried to become independent when ruler weak (c09).

answers.quote: Apart from his military campaigns, Dharmpala is also known for his patronage of Buddhism. He founded many Buddhist monasteries but, it was the famous Vikramshila University founded by him, that earned him a lot of fame.
answers.notes: Dharmapala-Vikramshila c17; Krishna I-Kailasha c50; Rajaraja I-Brihadishvara c52; Dantidurga-founder c49.

answers.quote: Gopala, who went on to become the founder of the Pala dynasty in Bengal, consolidated his rule over Bengal and brought the much needed stability and prosperity to the region.
answers.notes: Pala-Gopala c16; Pratihara-Nagabhatta I c44; Rashtrakuta-Dantidurga c49; Chola-Vijayalaya c51.

answers.quote: The first significant ruler of Bengal was Sasanka who ruled roughly between 606-637 A.D. Sasanka is considered the first historically known ruler of the area that constituted Bengal. He was also the first in this region to have extended his political sovereignty over areas that lay far beyond the geographical boundary of Bengal.
answers.notes: Sasanka 606-637 (c13); Gopala 8th c. (c46); Kaivarta revolt in later Pala sequence after Mahipala I (c24-c25); Lakshmanasena 1178 (c28) last. Kaivarta date is by claim sequence, not an explicit date, hence LIKELY.

answers.answer: A ও R দুটোই সঠিক এবং R হল A-এর সঠিক ব্যাখ্যা
answers.quote: Ever since Harshavardhana made Kanauj the capital of his empire, it remained the imperial centre of North Indian polities for several centuries, even though its political fortunes changed frequently.
answers.notes: Kanauj imperial centre since Harsha, fortunes changed frequently (c65); three powers fought for it (c18).

answers.quote: His court poet, Banabhatta, wrote his biography, the Harshacharita, in Sanskrit. This gives us the genealogy of Harsha, and ends with his becoming king.
answers.notes: Harshacharita is by Banabhatta (c01), not Ravikirti; pairs 1, 2, 4 match c57, c58, c60.
